blocks.text: Hadhrat Amrah reports that she once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "What would Rasulullaah ﷺ do at home?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was a human and would remove lice from his clothing, milk his goat and take care of himself."[^1]
Narrations of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) concerning the Humility of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ never assigned to anyone the duty of making arrangements for his wudhu and also the duty of handing out the charity he gave. He would personally attend to these duties.[^2]
Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to visit me, he was neither riding a mule nor a thoroughbred horse."[^3]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ performed Hajj on an old carriage (atop his camel) which was covered in a sheet that was hardly worth four Dirhams. Despite this, he prayed, 'O Allaah! Make this a Hajj devoid of ostentation and boastfulness.'"[^4]
The Humility of Rasulullaah ﷺ when he Victoriously Entered Makkah

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Makkah (upon the Conquest of Makkah) and the people were crowding to have a look at him, he placed his head against his carriage out of humility.[^5]
Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Makkah on the day Makkah was conquered, he had his chin on his carriage out of humility.[^6]

Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ reached Dhu Tuwa, he stood on his carriage. He wore his reddish, striped Yemeni shawl around his head with its end hanging over his face. When Rasulullaah ﷺ saw the great victory that Allaah had blessed him with, he lowered his head so much in humility to Allaah that his beard touched the centre of the carriage.[^7]
